newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SORRENTO DRIVES IN SEATTLE'S WINNING RUN OVER BOSTON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SORRENTO DRIVES IN SEATTLE'S WINNING RUN OVER BOSTON.

text.p: Paul Sorrento singled in Alex Rodriguez with the winning run in the 10th inning as the Seattle Mariners rallied for an 8-7 victory over the Boston Red Sox Sunday, salvaging the finale of the three-game series.
Rodriguez, who homered earlier in the game and had four hits, reached on an infield single and went to second on a wild pitch by Rick Trlicek (1-1).
Ken Griffey was intentionally walked and both runners were sacrificed by Rich Amaral. Jay Buhner was intentionally walked to load the bases.
Sorrento lined a 1-1 pitch into right, and Rodriguez trotted home with with his fourth run of the game.
"They loaded the bases to get an out an any base," Sorrento said. "As a hitter, it's definitely to your advantage."
Norm Charlton (1-1) got the win despite allowing a two-run game-tying single to ex-Mariner Darren Bragg in the ninth. He blew his second consecutive save opportunity.
Edgar Martinez had hit a two-run single and Sorrento a two-run double in the eighth to give the Mariners a 7-5 lead.

John Wasdin, acquired in the trade for Jose Canseco, allowed four runs and four hits over seven innings in his Boston debut, including Rodriguez's homer in the fourth and a two-run homer by Griffey, his fifth, in the sixth. Wasdin walked two and struck out a career-high nine batters.

In Anaheim, Brian Giles and Sandy Alomar homered in the ninth off closer Troy Percival (0-2) as the Cleveland Indians overcame a six-run deficit for a 10-8 victory over the Angels in the rubber game of their three-game series.
Percival, one of the league's dominant closers, is 0-3 lifetime against the Indians, allowing 10 earned runs in 13 1/3 innings.
Steve Kline (2-0) allowed one hit over three scoreless innings with a walk and two strikeouts for the win.
David Justice also homered for Cleveland in the second while Jim Edmonds and Garret Anderson homered in the first off Jack McDowell.
In Chicago, Jaime Navarro struck out a career-high 11 batters over seven shutout innings and Tony Phillips and Chris Snopek each hit solo homers as the White Sox defeated the Detroit Tigers, 5-3.
Navarro (1-0), who pitched for the crosstown Cubs last season, scattered five hits and two walks.
Chicago's bullpen made the game exciting, giving up three runs in the final two innings. Roberto Hernandez picked up his first save after he fanned Tony Clark with a runner on first.
Doug Brocail (0-1) was hammered for five runs and 10 hits in six innings.
At Minnesota, Mike Sweeney homered and drove in a career-high four runs as Glendon Rusch won his major-league debut and the Kansas Royals routed the Twins 12-2.
Sweeney hit a three-run homer in the fourth off Brad Radke (0-1) as the Royals built a 7-2 lead after five innings. Sweeney added an RBI single in the eighth.

Rusch, a 22-year-old left-hander who pitched last season for Triple-A Omaha, allowed two runs over eight innings, walking one and striking out four. Rusch allowed RBI doubles to Marty Cordova and Greg Colbrunn in a 37-pitch first inning before settling down.

In Oakland, Dave Telgheder and two relievers combined on a shutout as the Athletics scored all their runs on eighth-inning errors by third baseman Wade Boggs and first baseman Tino Martinez to defeat the New York Yankees 3-0.
Telgheder gave up six hits and two walks in 7 2/3 innings and has yet to give up a run in 10 2/3 innings this season.
Mark Acre (2-0) recorded the final out of the eighth. Billy Taylor pitched a 1-2-3 ninth for his third save.
Jeff Nelson (0-1) took the loss in relief of David Cone, who scattered two hits and three walks with nine strikeouts over seven innings.

In Texas, Rusty Greer had four hits, including an RBI double in a four-run first inning, as the Rangers pounded Mike Mussina (0-1) for seven runs and handed the Baltimore Orioles their first loss of the season, 9-3.
Dean Palmer drove in three runs for the Rangers.
Cal Ripken and Mickey Tettleton hit solo homers for the Orioles (4-1), the last major league team to lose in 1997.
Mussina was scratched from his Opening Day start due to a calcium deposit in his right elbow.
In Toronto, Jeff Cirillo drove in two runs and his seventh-inning double snapped a tie as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Blue Jays 3-2 to take the final two games of the three-game series.
Ben McDonald (1-1) allowed two runs over six innings for the win.
Doug Jones pitched a 1-2-3 ninth for his second save and 244th of his career, tying him for 10th place all-time with Dan Quisenberry.
